purpose: List events available to perf_events on this kernel — tracepoints, PMC events, software events. The first command to run when planning a perf session.

purpose: Count events without recording each one — the lowest-overhead perf mode. Default counts a basic CPU set; -e specifies events; -a is system-wide; -p targets a PID.

flags.name: -d
flags.doc: Detailed CPU counter statistics including extras.

flags.name: -e
flags.doc: Specific event(s). Supports tracepoints, PMCs, raw event specs (e.g. r003c).

purpose: Sample CPU stacks or trace specific events to a perf.data file for later analysis (perf report / perf script / FlameGraph generation). The workhorse for CPU profiling and tracepoint capture.

flags.name: -F
flags.doc: Sampling frequency in Hz (typical: 99 to avoid lockstep with timer interrupts).

flags.name: -g
flags.doc: Capture call graphs (stack traces) using frame pointers by default.

flags.name: --call-graph
flags.doc: Stack-walking method. fp needs frame pointers; dwarf is universal but heavier; lbr uses Last Branch Record.

flags.name: -e
flags.doc: Event to sample (tracepoint, raw PMC, etc.).

flags.name: -c
flags.doc: Sample period (one sample per N events). Use with PMC events like cache misses.

flags.name: --filter
flags.doc: Filter events by tracepoint variable predicate (e.g. 'rwbs == "WS"').

examples.expected_output: perf.data file with ~30s of all-CPU stack samples
examples.scenario: Standard system-wide CPU profile for FlameGraph generation

examples.expected_output: perf.data with PID stacks unwound via DWARF
examples.scenario: When the target wasn't built with frame pointers

examples.expected_output: Block I/O issue events with stack traces
examples.scenario: Disk-I/O-issuing code-path investigation
Off-CPU starting point — what's leaving CPU

examples.expected_output: Stack samples at every 100 last-level-cache misses
examples.scenario: Memory-stall investigation — where are LLC misses coming from
Profile a specific Docker container only

purpose: Display a perf.data file as a hierarchical (tree) summary with percentages. Default UI is the ncurses TUI; --stdio for text output. The default consumer of perf.data after perf record.

flags.name: --stdio
flags.doc: Text output instead of ncurses TUI.

flags.name: -g
flags.doc: Stack format: 'folded' = one line per stack (input shape for flamegraph.pl).

examples.expected_output: Interactive TUI with hot functions + drill-down
examples.scenario: Quick visual inspection of profile
Pipe into flamegraph.pl for FlameGraph generation

purpose: Dump every event from perf.data as text, one line per event with timestamp, comm, PID, stack. The raw form needed for custom post-processing (flame graphs, sequence analysis).

examples.scenario: Default text dump for piping to flamegraph stack-folding
Build precise CSV-ish input for downstream tools

purpose: Live top-N functions by sample count, refreshed continuously. Like top(1) but for code-paths instead of processes.

flags.name: -ns
flags.doc: -n shows sample count; -s sorts by given keys (e.g. comm,dso).

examples.scenario: Fast triage — what's the system spending CPU on right now
Process-level attribution view

purpose: Disassemble hot functions and overlay percentages from perf.data on each instruction. Shows precisely which line is hot inside a function.

examples.expected_output: Disassembly of recorded functions with sample %
examples.scenario: Pinpoint hot instruction in a hot function (needs debuginfo)

purpose: Add or remove dynamic tracepoints (kprobes/uprobes) at runtime. Lets you observe arbitrary kernel or user-space functions with arguments — without recompiling.

flags.name: --add
flags.doc: Create a probe (also implicit if no other action given).

flags.name: -V
flags.doc: Show available variables for that function (needs debuginfo).

flags.name: -L
flags.doc: Show line probes for the function (needs debuginfo).

purpose: Cache-line contention analysis (Linux 4.10+). Records and reports cache-line transfers between CPUs — the key signal for false-sharing and NUMA hot spots.

examples.scenario: 10-second system-wide cache-coherence capture
Identify false-sharing or NUMA-mishomed lines

purpose: strace-like tool built on perf_events — much lower overhead than strace because it uses perf's in-kernel buffer instead of ptrace.

examples.scenario: Latency-aware syscall trace without strace's order-of-magnitude slowdown

purpose: Attach a kprobe to a kernel function and run a BPF action block. The most common bpftrace shape for kernel-side dynamic tracing.

purpose: Timed sampling — fire on every CPU at the specified rate. Equivalent to perf record -F for sampling + bpftrace's expressive aggregations.

purpose: Trace new process creation via the exec() syscall. Prints PID, parent PID, comm, and full argv as each exec() fires. Essential for catching short-lived processes invisible to top/ps.

purpose: Per-event block I/O trace — comm, PID, disk, R/W, sector, bytes, latency for every I/O. The drill-down companion to biolatency's histogram.

examples.scenario: Attribute slow I/Os to specific processes after biolatency shows tail

purpose: Trace TCP connect() syscalls with PID, IP, and port. Captures outbound connection attempts that aren't visible via netstat-style snapshots.
